doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: 'Beyond the Sea', Don Lamond's fills and the Copa recording
summary: Don Lamond played on the record; Zito copied the fills and played the live Copa recording.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Ronnie, did you play on “Beyond the Sea” is that you on that record?
No man, that’s — I wish it was. That’s Don Lamond, the great Don Lamond man.
I always wanted to know who did those fills.

That’s Don Lamond. Only Don could do that. He was unbelievable. I got it down though man, when I was with Bobby, I played the same shit man. I practiced it, because I loved it so much that it was one of those things I said I’ve got to try to play this, I’ve got to do it. And in those days it was like I don’t know man, I was more fearless I think in those days.
Well that recording, the live concert that you’re on —
You talked about my son, he heard that many times man, because I played that recording many times. It’s just fantastic, Ronnie.
It’s a good record man, yeah.
As a matter of fact it’s hard to even listen to anybody else but you when you listen to that recording. I have to listen to you.
I’m like in front listening to the hi-hat and the —

Oh man, and they weren’t even my drums, man. I used to play on the drums, like we used to travel all over and I’d walk in and I would have maybe my own snare drum and that would be it. Everything else, whatever was there I played. And it was fine, it didn’t bother me, didn’t bother me at all.
